cases.title: A path that walks out of the target
cases.why: The classic zip-slip: the entry name contains `..`, so a naive reader writes beside the destination.
cases.message: error <archives>/traversal-parent.zip is not a zip archive zen can unpack — invalid relative path: ../../pwned.txt

cases.title: An absolute path
cases.why: `/etc/passwd` is not a project file, whatever the manifest says.
cases.message: error <archives>/traversal-absolute.zip is not a zip archive zen can unpack — absolute path: /etc/passwd

cases.title: A Windows separator in the name
cases.why: A reader that normalises `\` to `/` after checking the path has already lost the argument.
cases.message: error <archives>/traversal-backslash.zip is not a zip archive zen can unpack — invalid relative path: proj/../pwned

cases.title: An entry outside the manifest root
cases.why: The manifest names one directory; an entry from another one was not written by the exporter.
cases.message: error zzzz/xx.txt does not belong under proj/ — this archive was not written by `zen export`

cases.title: A symbolic link to /etc/passwd
cases.why: Writing a link is writing a path the extractor never checked.
cases.message: error proj/a.txt is a symbolic link — a link can point out of the directory being written to

cases.title: A symbolic link shaped like a directory
cases.why: The trailing slash makes a naive reader treat it as a directory entry, which is often skipped before the mode is checked.
cases.message: error proj/link/ is a symbolic link — a link can point out of the directory being written to

cases.title: A fifo that claims to be a file
cases.why: Only regular files and directories belong in a project archive. A fifo is a different kind of object and must not be materialised.
cases.message: error proj/fifo is not a regular file — this archive was not written by `zen export`

cases.title: A directory mode on a file name
cases.why: The type bits say directory and the name says file; the two disagree, so the entry is not trustworthy.
cases.message: error proj/weird is a directory entry without a trailing slash — this archive was not written by `zen export`

cases.title: An encrypted entry
cases.why: This tool does not write encrypted entries, so it cannot tell what this one contains.
cases.message: error proj/secret.txt is encrypted — zen does not write those

cases.title: An absurd number of file entries
cases.why: A central directory can ask for more work than a person would ever pack. It should be refused before the first file is created.
cases.message: error this archive holds more than 200000 entries

cases.title: An absurd number of directory entries
cases.why: Directory entries are not files, but they are still records in the central directory. A count that only counts files lets a flood through.
cases.message: error this archive holds more than 200000 entries

cases.title: An expansion bomb that declares more than 8 GiB
cases.why: The payload is a few bytes; the central directory claims gigabytes. The preflight must sum the claims before opening a decompressor.
cases.message: error this archive unpacks to more than 8 GiB

cases.title: A highly compressible payload below the limit
cases.why: This one is accepted by policy: the absolute byte bound is the defence, not a compression-ratio rule. The report records the residual risk.
cases.message: warning <run>/bomb-under-limit/landing has no agents.yaml — the archive did not hold a whole project

cases.title: Two names that differ only in case
cases.why: On macOS and Windows one entry silently overwrites the other; which one wins depends on extraction order.
cases.message: error proj/agents.yaml and proj/AGENTS.yaml differ only in case — a case-insensitive filesystem would overwrite one with the other

cases.title: Two spellings of the same Unicode name
cases.why: NFC and NFD are different bytes and the same name on a filesystem that normalises. Folding only case misses this.
cases.message: error proj/café.txt and proj/café.txt differ only in case — a case-insensitive filesystem would overwrite one with the other

cases.title: The same path twice
cases.why: The result depends on which entry the reader writes last, so the archive means different things to different readers.
cases.message: error this archive holds proj/a.txt twice — a case-insensitive filesystem would overwrite one with the other

cases.title: A path that is both a file and a directory
cases.why: Writing the file succeeds and writing below it fails with ENOTDIR, leaving a half-written tree.
cases.message: error proj/a/b is both a file and a directory in this archive

cases.title: A setuid bit on a regular file
cases.why: A mode is the archive's claim. The importer replaces it, so setuid cannot survive.
cases.message: warning <run>/mode-setuid/landing has no agents.yaml — the archive did not hold a whole project

cases.title: A file with no permission bits
cases.why: A zero mode is a valid claim but not a useful file; the importer decides the mode instead.
cases.message: warning <run>/mode-zero/landing has no agents.yaml — the archive did not hold a whole project

cases.title: A world-writable file
cases.why: A 0777 claim must not become a 0777 file.
cases.message: warning <run>/mode-world/landing has no agents.yaml — the archive did not hold a whole project

cases.title: An executable shell script
cases.why: A script has to be runnable to be useful, and that is the only bit the importer grants.
cases.message: warning <run>/mode-shell/landing has no agents.yaml — the archive did not hold a whole project

cases.title: A manifest that names a path outside the target
cases.why: The root and the name are used to build paths and registry keys, so they are checked rather than trusted.
cases.message: error zenera-export.json names the project in a way zen will not write

cases.title: A benign entry before a hostile one
cases.why: If the guard runs while writing, the benign file is already on disk when the hostile entry is refused.
cases.message: error <archives>/partial-write.zip is not a zip archive zen can unpack — invalid relative path: ../../pwned.txt

cases.title: Names Windows cannot represent safely
cases.why: A Linux import accepts these, then a Windows checkout has to deal with them. The report records them as residual risk rather than claiming they are safe.
cases.message: warning <run>/windows-names/landing has no agents.yaml — the archive did not hold a whole project

cases.title: Directory entries with no files
cases.why: An empty directory is not part of the project; the archive is accepted and the directory does not travel.
cases.message: warning <run>/empty-dirs/landing has no agents.yaml — the archive did not hold a whole project
